features.rationale: Native options are explicitly selected. Aggregate mapping does not claim every option exists; unmapped option behavior remains review work.

Core optional paths and model strings retain upstream values without configuration-time validation. Omitted cli_path is discovered in Python's order at startup (golden argv, environment and initialize bytes are pinned by tests/golden_argv_env.rs); Windows batch paths are refused before spawn. Named fixtures cover argument preservation and cwd forwarding, not upstream runtime parity. The bundled executable lookups (Python _bundled directory, TypeScript platform packages with musl and Windows or arm variants) are caller-driven helpers in find_bundled_cli and find_native_cli; they are not part of connect's discovery. Python's bundled-CLI version gate (999.0.0 minimum, claude.version record) and its derived client app trigger are the same kind of helper, meets_derived_client_app_minimum and bundled_cli_derives_client_app; connect asks them only through the Python-dialect client_app_derivation option, so TypeScript, which has neither, stays connect's default.

Process errors carry Python's message, the exit code and the TypeScript text; an exit after an error result becomes ResultError (Python text, or the TypeScript text when non-empty); spawn failures split into missing executable, missing cwd and other; AbortError ends an aborted run. Close escalates stdin close, SIGTERM, SIGKILL. Writes follow upstream order: after an exit Python reports the terminated process with its exit code and TypeScript reports not ready; the exited-with-error branch is unreachable in both SDKs. Writes fail with distinct variants (not ready, terminated process, write failure, aborted) instead of DriverStopped. JSON decode errors carry the line and the original error (Python style; TypeScript style skips undecodable lines) and message parse errors carry the raw data.

The exact default/acceptEdits/plan/bypassPermissions/dontAsk/auto literals round-trip, and unknown modes are forwarded unchanged without Rust-side validation. None omits the CLI flag; Some(Default) emits default explicitly. Fixtures establish serialization and argument behavior, not the CLI permission policy.

Exact user/project/local literals and optional ordered lists preserve omission, empty lists and duplicates. None omits --setting-sources; Some([]) emits --setting-sources=. Pinned Python docs and TypeScript Options docs describe inheritance on omission and filesystem isolation for an empty list. Skills-driven defaults and live CLI behavior are outside this scoped mapping.

Rust follows Python lifecycle names with an async connect factory and consuming async disconnect(self), rather than methods on an existing Python client. TypeScript Query.close is the cleanup counterpart. Memory-process fixtures require initialization before returning an owner and verify the child input is closed on disconnect; named references alone do not prove test execution or native conformance.
Rust separates process ownership, cloneable controls and message consumption. Only explicitly mapped operations have focused evidence.
query follows a full run; query_turn exposes the first-result boundary. Fixture evidence covers background continuation and coalesced queued input; live inference remains separate.
Streaming and queued structured sends are exposed through a cloneable handle. Completion semantics use reported queue/session state and have older-CLI limits.
Typed Rust receipts preserve legacy absence and reported queue/cancel metadata; no exact Python return-type equivalence is intended.

Dynamic updates preserve existing same-name embedded sessions; remove and re-add to replace a registry. The reply is kept as the CLI sent it, None where TypeScript returns undefined, and {} for anything but an object under ArgvStyle::Python.

The initialize request matches sdk.mjs 0.3.323 byte for byte by default (request id, envelope order, hooks, matcher, timeout and onFailure spelling, jsonSchema, systemPrompt, appendSystemPrompt, supportedDialogKinds) and claude_agent_sdk 0.2.181 under ArgvStyle::Python (req_N_hex ids, hooks null, matcher null, json.dumps spelling). The response is read without validation like both SDKs: typed fields of an unexpected type read as absent, as_json keeps the value as sent (Python style reads a non-object as an empty object), and the TypeScript checks run in its order: blocking hooks need hook_on_failure_supported, a first initialize with blocking hooks fails on hooks_applied false, managed settings need managed_settings_applied, and unconfirmed plugins log a warning. initializationResult, supportedModels, supportedAgents and accountInfo read the cached response like sdk.mjs; supportedCommands prefers the latest commands_changed list; reinitialize sends a non-first initialize and replaces the cache.

Explicit typed Rust option is wired to CLI arguments or initialization. Fixture proves configuration transport; native inference behavior is not inferred. The Python dialect spells the amount as str(float) does, checked against CPython over a corpus that includes the shortest-digit ties (usd_budget_goldens.py writes the goldens).

Rust represents background execution and names with enums/value objects. Core agent initialization is tested; aggregate declaration equality is not assumed.

can_use_tool answers match sdk.mjs 0.3.323 and claude_agent_sdk 0.2.181 byte for byte in each ArgvStyle. TypeScript appends toolUseID, keeps decisionClassification, writes nothing for AnsweredOutOfBand, still writes a cancelled handler's answer and skips a redelivered in-flight request id; Python echoes the original input on allow, rejects a null result with its TypeError text, drops a cancelled handler without a response and runs a redelivered id twice (DuplicateControlRequests::RunBoth, opt-in). A missing handler is answered with each SDK's own error text. CLI rules can authorize before consulting the host.

ToolPermissionRequest carries every TypeScript canUseTool option (decisionReasonType, decisionReasonCode, serverPolicyAskOnly, plugin, serverPrompt, computerFolder, matchedAskRule and the rest) and the Python ToolPermissionContext fields. Lenient fields are read only when well typed, as sdk.mjs does, and a value of the wrong type stays in additional_fields instead of being dropped. PermissionDecision covers PermissionResult allow/deny with updatedInput, updatedPermissions, interrupt and decisionClassification, plus the null result (AnsweredOutOfBand). Updates are written in each SDK's key order (TypeScript type/fields/destination, Python to_dict type/destination/fields). A Python PermissionUpdate without a destination is sent through PermissionUpdate::Unknown with its raw object, which reproduces to_dict's bytes.

Hook routing, cancellation (HookContext.signal is HookRequest.signal) and fail-closed blocking registration match upstream. HookRequest.typed_input decodes every input into the upstream HookInput union, and HookOutput.Json sends any upstream HookJSONOutput, sync or async, exactly as given, so no event-specific field is narrowed or dropped.

HookEvent.ALL lists every event in the order upstream HOOK_EVENTS does, and HOOK_EVENTS, EXIT_REASONS and ExitReason are generated from the pinned declarations; an exit reason upstream adds later decodes as ExitReason.Unknown, and a new event still requires review.

Every event input, its base fields and effort, every hook-specific output and both sync and async output shapes are generated from the pinned TypeScript declarations with undeclared keys kept in order. Python TypedDicts declare the same wire keys, so one set of types serves both.

The handler sees every mode the CLI sends (ElicitationMode::Other keeps unknown ones) and the request id. Answers match sdk.mjs 0.3.323 byte for byte: AnsweredOutOfBand writes nothing, no handler declines. claude_agent_sdk 0.2.181 has no elicitation handler and answers with its unsupported-subtype error in the Python dialect.

As in sdk.mjs 0.3.323, supportedDialogKinds is only advertised in initialize and every request_user_dialog reaches the handler whatever its kind. AnsweredOutOfBand and a missing handler write nothing; a redelivered in-flight id is skipped. claude_agent_sdk 0.2.181 has no dialog handler and answers with its unsupported-subtype error in the Python dialect.

LocalMcpServer answers the JSON-RPC surface of the server each SDK helper builds: initialize with protocol negotiation, ping, tools/list, tools/call and request cancellation, with the same envelopes and error shapes. McpServerDialect::TypeScript, the default, follows createSdkMcpServer: unreadable messages are dropped, parameter errors are -32603 zod issue lists, schemas are listed with their draft-07 $schema, and instructions, alwaysLoad and searchHint are answered. McpServerDialect::Python follows create_sdk_mcp_server over the mcp package: unreadable messages surface as McpServerError::Protocol, requests before initialize are refused, a cancelled call is answered with -32800, annotations keep the standard hints and SdkTools::with_duplicates keeps repeated names. In the Python dialect a JSON-RPC id round-trips as json.loads and json.dumps keep it: integers of any size and -0 are echoed exactly, strings are echoed, and floats, booleans, null and nested values are not request ids, so a found server acknowledges them without an id while a missing server echoes json.dumps(json.loads(id)). Both helpers register only tools, so resources, prompts and server-initiated client requests belong to custom SdkMcpServer implementations. Argument checks reproduce the upstream messages for type, required, enum, const, items and string or number bounds; other schema keywords report the Rust validator's message.

Every TypeScript stdio, sse, http and instance-less sdk config field is typed, sent in declaration order and followed by caller keys verbatim, in caller insertion order. URLs are kept verbatim; McpUrl::validated is an opt-in check neither SDK performs. TypeScript style leaves in-process servers out of --mcp-config and names them in initialize sdkMcpServers; Python style lists them as sdk entries with json.dumps formatting, and ClaudeAgentOptions::mcp_config carries Python's str or Path form verbatim. An in-process server replaces an external config of the same name, and set_mcp_servers is not serialized, as in TypeScript.

Rust implements append/load/list_sessions/list_session_summaries/list_subkeys/delete, an upstream-equivalent conformance suite, and summary folding in both the TypeScript (default) and Python layouts. Optional operations are declared through SessionStore::supports because Rust cannot detect trait method overrides. Wall time and transcript filesystem operations can be replaced through static adapters; memory fixtures cover resume materialization, cleanup of the temporary directory and removal of a partially written temporary directory on failure.

Store-backed resume follows both upstream SDKs, selected by SessionStoreOptions.dialect with TypeScript as the default: TypeScript continue takes only the newest listed session, preserves source modes on copied auth files, writes settings at 0600, fails on unreadable credentials, derives the project key from options.env or the process environment as Wn does, and sets CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR on Windows; Python walks newest first past sidechains and unusable candidates and skips unreadable optional files. Both accept a relative configuration or home directory as given unless SessionStoreOptions::require_absolute_config_paths is set, and a TypeScript resume writes every listSubkeys subpath its check lets through. Materialization runs on every platform, and project keys over 200 characters are truncated with the upstream hash suffix. Resume entry, byte and subkey limits are opt-in and unlimited by default, and the transcript mirror reports every failure and waits for a flush without a deadline unless SessionStoreLimits sets max_retained_failures or flush_timeout; custom stores declare optional operations through SessionStore::supports.
Rust validates text/image/document/tool-result input and permits explicit future extensions; upstream message types also contain output/history details beyond the prompt constructor.

Every message keeps its exact wire object in raw, and to_sdk_message returns the generated upstream::messages type for it, so identity, origin, stop, terminal, model usage, permission denial and nested usage fields are typed as sdk.d.ts declares them. The corpus goldens from the pinned TypeScript and Python query() pin both views.

MessageDecoding::TypeScript, the default, yields every message the pinned TypeScript query() yields, unknown types and shapes Rust cannot type included, as Message::Unknown with the raw object, and consumes keep_alive. MessageDecoding::Python skips unknown types and raises the KeyError and type errors Python parse_message raises, with its texts.

Every member of the pinned SDKMessage union, the hook started, progress and response messages included, and the active_goal message the TypeScript query() also yields are generated from the pinned declarations together with every type their fields name, with undeclared keys kept in order so encoding reproduces the message. NonNullableUsage and the other types the declarations import from the Anthropic API package stay JSON objects, as they reach TypeScript.

McpDiscovery::CliDefault is the default, so MCP discovery follows the CLI as in both upstream SDKs; --strict-mcp-config is sent only when McpDiscovery::Disabled is selected, as upstream sends it only for strictMcpConfig / strict_mcp_config.

EnvironmentMode exposes both upstream behaviors. The default, TypeScript, replaces the inherited environment with options.env when it has entries and inherits otherwise, as sdk.mjs does; Replace and Inherit select either branch explicitly (Replace covers an explicit empty options.env), and Overlay merges options.env over the inherited environment as Python does. Injectable environment providers control SDK lookups. The Python-dialect client_app_derivation option reproduces CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DERIVED_CLIENT_APP with the same trigger (a bundled CLI whose pin and recorded claude.version are at least 999.0.0), the same variable and the same name/version format, but names the application with this crate's package name and version because Rust has no Python distribution metadata to look up; TypeScript derives none, which is the default. An explicit client_app is written as CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP over options.env, as Python writes it, in every environment mode.

All eleven session functions are exposed in both forms: filesystem (SessionFiles methods and free functions) and store-backed (the *_from_store readers, *_via_store mutations and import_session_to_store). Each takes the TypeScript or Python dialect, TypeScript by default: the *_with store helpers and the TypeScript filesystem readers reproduce includeSystemMessages, includeProgrammatic, continued-in sessions, custom-title sidecars, worktree ownership checks, the chain and relink algorithm and the store-backed listSessions, checked against fixtures generated from the pinned bundle. Forked entries keep JSON.stringify key order, the Python dialect escapes non-ASCII as json.dumps does, and custom stores declare optional operations through SessionStore::supports. Core storage operations are mapped separately.

settings (path, JSON text or Settings object), sandbox, managedSettings and managedSettingsDelivery are wired for both dialects and checked against argv and initialize bytes captured from the real TypeScript bundle and Python package. TypeScript serializes objects with JSON.stringify semantics and merges the sandbox into the settings document (a settings file path together with a sandbox is refused, unparseable settings text is replaced); Python reads the settings file relative to the working directory, replaces the sandbox key and writes json.dumps text. Managed settings reach the CLI by argv or the initialize request and are ignored by the Python dialect. Known differences: Python JSON decode error wording follows serde_json, an invalid managedSettingsDelivery is unrepresentable, initialize managedSettings numbers at or above 2^63 or written in exponent form may differ from JavaScript, and the managed-settings confirmation hold and timeout framework belongs to the initialize control work. The settings resolution, flag settings and updateSettings surfaces are mapped separately.

Exact argv, in the upstream order of each dialect. TypeScript uses --flag=value; Python uses two tokens except --resume, --session-id, --resume-session-at, --resume-drops-turn and --setting-sources. thinking wins over max_thinking_tokens; TypeScript sends maxThinkingTokens 0 as --thinking=disabled and an enabled config without a budget as --thinking=adaptive, while Python rejects it with the upstream KeyError text. The callback and permission_prompt_tool_name are mutually exclusive with dialect-specific text; the callback otherwise selects --permission-prompt-tool stdio. TypeScript refuses a fallback model equal to the model; Python does not. The TypeScript-only options permission_prompts, channels, debug, debug_file, allow_dangerously_skip_permissions and project_config_root are ignored by the Python dialect. The derived per-process debug file is added for connect() in the TypeScript dialect when no debug_file is set. skills appends Skill or Skill(name) to the allowed tools (TypeScript dedupes against the caller list only, Python against the growing list), Python defaults --setting-sources=user,project, and an explicit list also reaches the initialize request. The Python Windows metacharacter check applies to the resume and session options. The can-use-tool shadow advisory goes through tracing in both dialects. TypeScript surrogate and non-string skill name checks are unreachable because Rust strings are valid Unicode; channels has no declaration in the TypeScript types and follows the bundle.

TypeScript passes --plugin-dir=PATH or --plugin-dir-no-mcp=PATH per plugin, or with pluginDelivery initialize and at least one plugin passes --await-initialize and sends the plugins in the initialize request; Python passes the two-token --plugin-dir PATH and has no delivery option, so PluginDelivery is ignored with ArgvStyle::Python. The upstream 'Invalid pluginDelivery' and 'Unsupported plugin type' errors cannot occur because the Rust types admit only the valid variants.

Every request matches sdk.mjs 0.3.323 byte for byte, captured from the published package with JSON.stringify number spelling, optional fields omitted when unset and the same request ids. Replies keep the value the CLI sent (ControlReply::as_json), None when the reply has no response where TypeScript returns undefined, with the generated upstream type available through decode, and each method returns what the TypeScript method returns: readFile is None on any failure, setMcpPermissionModeOverride is {} for an absent response, backgroundTasks is true for an absent backgrounded. A rejection keeps its error_code when it matches the TypeScript pattern. backgroundTasks refuses a non-boolean backgrounded where TypeScript returns it untyped. Python 0.2.181 has none of these methods.

The public Transport trait is Python's Transport (connect, write, read_message in place of read_messages, close, is_ready, end_input) with a provided kill for TypeScript's abort. ClaudeSdkClient::connect_with_transport, query_with_transport and query_turn_with_transport inject one; the subprocess implementation is the default and the SpawnProcess adapter stays TypeScript's spawnClaudeCodeProcess. A custom transport gets no CLI discovery, argument list or store-backed resume materialization (the mirror still runs), as upstream.

WebSocketTransport is the browser SDK's WebSocket transport as a Transport implementation, replayed against goldens recorded by running the real class in node (websocket_transport_goldens.mjs): the auth line is sent first, a keep_alive line every 50000ms while the driver reads, inbound text frames are split on newlines with partial lines kept, bad JSON dropped and ccr_event removed, writes go out verbatim, close sends 1000 Normal closure, close codes other than 1000 and 1001 fail with the upstream text, the connect timeout is 15000ms, abort and a not-ready write carry the upstream messages. headers is accepted and ignored by default like the browser class; HeaderDelivery::Handshake opts into sending them on the upgrade request. JSON values that are not objects are dropped because Transport yields objects. The query-level browser options (websocket, sse), SSE and the rest of the browser entrypoint stay out of scope.

tool_use_result keeps any JSON value with omission distinct from null, which is what both pinned SDKs pass through on the wire; tool_use_result_object gives the dictionary view Python annotates. The goldens include list and null results.

StreamEvent.to_sdk_message types ttft_ms, user_message_uuid, user_message_uuids and resume_reason as sdk.d.ts declares them, raw keeps the exact envelope, and the goldens pin the stream_event corpus against both pinned SDKs.

Settings is generated from the pinned declarations: all 182 declared top-level keys, every nested object, string-literal union and object union, the $schema key and the open index signature. Unknown keys and key order survive a decode then encode byte for byte, and a string-literal value upstream does not list is kept. Nothing is validated. Python has no Settings type; its settings option is a path or JSON string, which SettingsInput distinguishes explicitly. Wiring Settings into Options.settings is mapped separately. Hook handler kinds, marketplace and plugin sources, statusLine, sshConfigs, enabledPlugins and pluginConfigs are generated unions: a union picks the member that re-encodes to the same JSON with the fewest undeclared keys and unlisted string-literal values, so a discriminant selects its own member, and anything else is kept as raw JSON.

TypeScript declares the sandbox types as Zod inferences, which equal the generated sandbox property of Settings (16 keys, open object); the Rust names alias those types. Python SandboxSettings and SandboxNetworkConfig TypedDicts use a subset of the same keys, and fixtures show them re-encoding byte for byte. Python has no filesystem or credentials TypedDict, so those are TypeScript only.

The result, option and error shapes of resolveSettings are generated from the pinned declarations and keep unknown keys and unlisted source names. The resolveSettings function itself is mapped separately. Python has no equivalent types.

resolve_settings runs the platform readers (plutil, reg query, WSL reg.exe, /etc/claude-code) behind the SettingsHost adapter traits and matches the pinned TypeScript resolver byte for byte on 54 fixture trees (mise run claude-sdk:resolve-diff), including the read path of normal settings files (pre-parse sanitizers, managed-only key removal, document key order). Partial until the listed gap closes: the policy-tolerant schema for managed settings (catch substitutions and entry salvage). The MDM re-read throttle follows the pinned state machine against the host clock, with a re-read its caller does not wait for running on a thread of its own (fixtures replay it, slow reads included, with a fake clock). Numbers read as JSON.parse reads them: integers above 2^53 round, and a token past the double range reads as Infinity, which typed settings refuse, env values spell with String() as z.coerce.string() does, and the resolver prints as null. js_stringify prints resolved settings exactly as JSON.stringify does (checked against Node over a corpus of doubles and documents). The Python dialect reads files as json.loads reads them, and resolve_python_settings returns integers of any size exactly and floats with their type, so python_json_dumps prints them as json.dumps does (checked against CPython over a corpus of doubles, documents and refused text). Python has no equivalent.

Initialize bytes (key order, omitted undefined fields, kept false, empty string, empty list and empty object) and the Python system prompt flags are asserted against output captured from sdk.mjs 0.3.323 and claude-agent-sdk 0.2.181 for 31 option cases. The runtime-only TypeScript options (appendSubagentSystemPrompt, codeRunningMcpTools, webSearchIsolationExemptMcpServers, rapidFollowupPreempt, forwardNestedSubagentToolCalls, workspaceTrust, captureSdkMcpManifests) are absent from sdk.d.ts and are mapped by Rust API only. TypeScript-only fields are not sent with ArgvStyle::Python, which sends only excludeDynamicSections, systemPromptSnapshot and forwardSubagentText when true. captureSdkMcpManifests has no consumer until SDK MCP manifests are captured; ClaudeAgentOptions::captures_sdk_mcp_manifests resolves its default.

toolConfig, getOAuthToken, getHostAuthToken, workload, executable and executableArgs, and the load timeout texts are pinned to goldens recorded from the TypeScript 0.3.323 bundle; ArgvStyle::Python answers both token refreshes with the Python unsupported-subtype error even when a handler is set, and the Python timeout wording is selected by argv_style. debug_stderr is an upstream no-op, so the Rust field is accepted and ignored. add_dirs, user and max_buffer_size map to additional_directories, user and limits.max_buffer_size. Known limits: a host token handler returns a string or none, never the bare number the bundle would forward, and token callbacks use the opt-in callback_timeout limit.

Argv tokens and order, the dash rule, extraArgs dictionary semantics (duplicate keys collapse, TypeScript lists integer keys first), the tools preset, empty agent and resume, stderr delivery (raw decoder chunks for TypeScript, trimmed lines for Python), max_buffer_size including zero, client_app precedence and the sessionStore with persistSession false refusal are pinned against goldens captured from the real sdk.mjs 0.3.323 and claude-agent-sdk 0.2.181 driving a recording stand-in for the CLI. user resolves the name with getpwnam and switches only the real and effective uid with setreuid in a pre_exec hook, as CPython does; debug_stderr is an accepted no-op.
The adaptive, enabled and disabled thinking shapes reach the argv in each SDK's spelling, with the display option on the two shapes that take one.
The total token budget is sent as the task budget argument in both orderings.
Python sandbox dictionaries map onto the typed sandbox settings and replace the settings sandbox key with json.dumps bytes.
Stdio, SSE, HTTP and in-process server options encode to the exact mcp config bytes of each SDK.
The status reply decodes into typed server entries carrying every key the Python TypedDicts declare.
Every key the Python response declares is typed, and undeclared keys stay in additional_fields.
Session metadata is read from files and from a store into the same typed info.
Store entries, listing rows and the flush mode have typed Rust forms exercised through the store helpers.
The transport trait answers connect, write, read, close, is_ready and end_input and drives a whole session.
Tool name, description, schema, handler and annotations are replayed against the Python server answers.
Custom, file and preset prompts and the tools preset reach the argv in each dialect.
Destinations, behaviors and rule values round-trip through the permission update wire form.
Constructor texts are asserted against strings recorded from the Python error classes.
The first-party names each Python module imports are reachable from the crate root.
